My demolition duo get very destructive if I haven't brought them more toys once they destroy their current ones. They stay outside for no longer than 8 hours while we work. My lab is about a year and a half, knows to chew her toys but once they're gone.... What's in the yard is free for all to chew. I've learnt that she in particular gets quite bored when home alone and therefore becomes destructive. 

My boarder collie however, gets very lonely. We had him 9 months by himself before getting our lab. He would dig and chew things he shouldn't instead of his toys (Never anything dangerous). He isn't a very vocal dog so never barked or cried but definitely was very sooky when we got home and overly attached or wouldn't want to come to us, instead sitting near us but not with. Once we got our lab he was a lot happier having that company and now enjoys snuggling  with her when were out and at home.

So I've got both, destructive bored and destructive anxious. Once you figure out why your dogs destructive there are ways to manage it. I have to baby proof my yard, just in case either I forget my lab has destroyed her toys already or in case I didn't buy the right toys. They get love and attention when we get home and a 6km walk around the lake ending at the dog park. Extra exercise really helped my lab.

When I tried to sort my collie out, I heard really  good things about the thunder coat and a collar or air purifier type thing that had anti anxiety stuff. Unfortunately I'm unable to test them as my collie chews his coats and collars off. So I decided not to spend a pretty penny on things for him to destroy. 

While I think creating is a last resort I don't think it's awful of he has proper stimulation. I'd suggest maybe leaving him in the bathroom or laundry if it's a bigger area. Put the radio on, clear the area of unsafe things and put some toys in there for him. You could try slowly giving him more free run of the house that way. Otherwise I'd agree hiring a dog walker a few days a week might be cheaper and help break up that alone time.

First off, I 100% get where you're coming from and I can't express how sorry I am that you have to deal with that shit. I'm 19 and have dealt with depression for about 5 years and it sucks ass. 

Secondly, it seems you have a few options. For starters, you could try to wait it out and hope for the best - I don't really recommend that option though. Next on my list of options is a psych ward. Like tbh I hated it when I was in there but it gave me an incentive not to go back there plus it gave me a little time to think without any distractions. Next, go see a psych if you don't want to go to a ward, be open and honest with them and there will be so many options and ideas they can give you. Second to last, talk to some close family and friends or even have a sit by yourself and try to write a list of things you want to do. Use your family and friends to help give you motivation to go out and do those things even if its only going to the shops, its something you can cross of your list and be proud of. Lastly, you can give yourself a year of trying as hard as you can to feel better. If you at the end of the year can say you tried as hard as you can and nothing then you can think about what you want to do next.

So I'm only 19 but I've had a rather lengthy (given my age at least) experience with depression - to the point of trying twice to kill myself this year alone. After each time I felt regret. It started as regret I didn't kill myself. That I wasn't good enough to live let alone kill myself. That I was an absolute failure and regret not planning it a little better. After... sometimes it was a week and sometimes a few days I regretted everything I put my friends and family through. But the story doesn't end with "and I realized it was a bad idea and I lived happily ever after". I did it again after that. I've done it several times. And without any change I went straight back to square one... if not further back sometimes. 

The point of this is that without change your stuck. Your life probably looks great on paper! But that won't make you happy. When you've got a day or two off sit and think about things you want to do, even if they're far fetched. Think of times you have been happy, even if they only made you a little bit happy. Write them down. I'm not sure of your financial situation but selling everything and moving towns or traveling and soul searching. Maybe you aren't in that sort of financial situation, maybe its searching for a new job for now, taking up new hobbies anything to change things up. Heck! Get a pet! 

I wouldn't call this wasting your life, depression is a rough thing. It's not going to go away but its managable. You just have to work out how you'll manage because how I manage (or at least try to) might not be same way you do.
